task_statement:
Research question (as posed on 2026-10-06, in the area of defensive suppression and counter strategy (best/avoid)):
A defense's effect on opponents' H2-H1 change is a reliable team trait.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): 120 team-seasons

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

methodological_questions: regression to the mean in half-to-half changes

historical_evidence.finding: Split-half reliability of Connector teammate-path quality Q_p (a player-level half-to-half metric) was r=0.215, Spearman-Brown 0.355, ICC=0.216, and was too low to treat Q_p as a stable scoutable trait. Most variance was within-player half-to-half.

Ranked playsheet validation using H2-H1 PPP drops (>=0.25) found no full-rank Spearman signal (rho=-0.06, p=0.10) and was limited by leakage, low measurement reliability, and small sample. A trigger accuracy rho=0.45 was observed but overall inconclusive.

Foul-trouble sequencing after a star's 2nd foul showed an apparent opponent PPP rise that was an artifact of free throw share (41.8% vs 9.9%); after removing free throws the effect was not significant.
Possession Control Index incremental R2 over ORtg was an artifact; the headlined gain was leakage tracking DRtg, and offensive-control added only +0.005 R2.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Split-half reliability of a player-level half-to-half metric (Q_p) using odd/even game halves.
failed_approaches.why: Measurement reliability was too low (split-half r=0.215, SB 0.355); the metric was not stable enough to be a trait.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Using H2-H1 PPP drops to trigger ranked playsheet predictions (BEST > AVOID).
failed_approaches.why: Inconclusive results due to leakage, low measurement reliability, and small sample; no clear full-rank signal emerged.

evidence_establishes: Player-level half-to-half metrics can suffer from very low split-half reliability (r~0.2), making them unsuitable as stable traits.
Half-to-half changes are noisy and can be confounded by artifacts (e.g., free throw share) if not carefully adjusted.
evidence_does_not_establish: Whether team-level aggregation of opponent H2-H1 change yields sufficient reliability to be a team trait.
The true underlying stability of a defensive team's effect on opponent H2-H1 adjustments.
The magnitude of any such defensive effect.
own_inferences: Team-level aggregation over 41+ games per half-season may increase reliability compared to a player-level half-to-half metric, but inherent game-to-game variability in adjustments may still limit the signal.

Even modest reliability (e.g., ICC ~0.3-0.4) could be detectable with 120 team-seasons, but would not support a strong claim of a 'reliable team trait' without a pre-specified high threshold (e.g., ICC > 0.5).
Confounding by opponent offensive strength, game script, and team tactics may further dilute the defensive signal.
uncertainties: The true split-half reliability for an aggregated team-level opponent H2-H1 change metric.
Optimal adjustment for opponent quality, venue, and half-time score effects.
Cross-season stability given roster turnover, coaching changes, and scheme evolution.
Influence of including partial 2025-26 data or playoff games on the reliability estimate.

historical_effect.explanation: The historical evidence of very low reliability for a player-level half-to-half metric ([prior work][prior work]) directly warns that similar metrics may be too noisy. This shifted the initial assessment from a naive proceed to a careful design with pre-registered reliability thresholds and rigorous controls, because a naive correlation test without these safeguards would risk a false claim of a reliable trait.

blocking_constraints.text: Opponent H2-H1 change per game is inherently noisy; the true split-half reliability at the team level may be well below 0.5, making it difficult to establish as a stable trait even with 120 team-seasons.

The defensive effect on opponent second-half change is likely confounded by opponent offensive strength, home/away status, game script (blowouts, resting starters), and team offensive output, requiring many control variables that may reduce effective power.
If most teams have near-zero true effect, the reliability estimate will be dominated by noise, and a null finding of no reliability is a weak statement.

prior_work.summary: Prior project work found that a player-level half-to-half metric (Q_p) had very low split-half reliability and was untestable as a stable trait. This suggests caution but does not directly address a team-level defensive effect on opponent H2-H1 change.

risks.text: The measurement reliability of opponent H2-H1 change is likely low, and split-half correlations may be too weak to support a claim of a reliable team trait without a very large sample.
Confounding by opponent strength, game location, score effects, and team offensive performance is expected and may obscure the true defensive signal.
The true between-team variance in H2-H1 adjustment may be small, diminishing the practical significance even if statistically detectable.
Defensive schemes, coaching staffs, and rosters change across seasons, so reliability over multiple years may be eroded by non-stationarity.

design.estimand: Team-level split-half reliability (ICC and Spearman-Brown adjusted Pearson r) of opponent H2-H1 points per 100 possessions, adjusted for opponent offensive rating, venue, and game number, using the first 41 games vs. last 41 games of the regular season.
design.unit: team-season (each team's complete 82-game regular season, or as many as available, excluding partial seasons)
design.sample: All complete team-seasons from 2022-23 through 2025-26 regular seasons (approx. 120 team-seasons). Exclude playoffs and the 2025-26 partial regular season before 2026-04-13. Exclude team-seasons with fewer than 60 games.
design.power: For n=120, power >0.80 to detect a split-half correlation of rho=0.25 (two-tailed alpha=0.05). If true rho <=0.20, the study will likely be inconclusive; this will be interpreted as insufficient evidence for a reliable trait.
design.controls: Raw opponent H2-H1 PPP difference per game (or possession-adjusted) will be regressed on: opponent season ORtg, home/away indicator, pre-game team defensive rating, half-time score margin, back-to-back indicator, and a team fixed effect. The residual (or team-level mean residual) will be used for reliability analysis.
design.falsification: A Spearman-Brown adjusted correlation below 0.30 and a lower 95% CI crossing zero will be treated as a rejection of the hypothesis of a reliable trait. A permutation test shuffling team labels will be used to confirm that any observed correlation is not due to chance clustering.
design.multiplicity: A single primary reliability metric (adjusted opponent H2-H1 change) is defined a priori. Exploratory analyses (by quarter, by play type) will be reported with Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
design.decision_rule: Reject the null of no reliability if the Spearman-Brown adjusted correlation is >0.50 AND the lower bound of its 95% CI is >0.20. Otherwise, conclude the evidence is insufficient to claim a reliable team trait, regardless of the p-value.
design.data_version: NBA per-game data from stats API as frozen on 2026-10-06; regular-season data only for 2022-23, 2023-24, 2024-25, and the completed 2025-26 regular season.
